overview.location: Gaj Pass (4,164m) is a remote Dhauladhar crossing above Kangra district connecting the Ghera Valley with the Lamdal forest zone in the Ravi watershed. The approach starts from Ghera village — accessible from Dharamshala. The HP TMS itinerary passes through Rawa, Bonthu, and Bagga shepherd hamlets before the pass, with Lamdal ('forest and mountain') as the final destination.
overview.history: The Gaddi shepherd community has used the Gag Pass route for seasonal migration for generations — crossing between the Kangra Valley winter pastures and summer grazing in the Ravi watershed. The HP government registered this route (trek ID 67) specifically to bring safety monitoring to this remote corridor used by increasingly adventurous independent trekkers.
overview.length: 32 km over 4 days. Day 1: Ghera to Rawa–Bonthu (8 km). Day 2: Bonthu to Bagga night camp (8 km). Day 3: Bagga to Gag Pass to Lamdal (9 km). Day 4: Lamdal return (7 km to road). Total elevation gain to pass: approximately 2,500m from valley floor.
overview.temperature: Apr–Jun: 0°C–15°C at pass; snow reducing; spring flowers on lower slopes. Sep–Oct: –2°C to 12°C; clearest visibility; recommended. Jul–Aug: Monsoon rain on the Kangra slope; trail slippery. Nov–Mar: Pass blocked per HP TMS.
overview.fitness: Hard. Remote with no infrastructure beyond shepherd camps. Self-sufficiency with tent required at multiple camps per HP TMS. The 4,164m pass requires sustained fitness. A local guide familiar with this route is recommended.

itinerary.title: Dharamshala → Ghera → Rawa → Bonthu
itinerary.desc: Drive to Ghera. Register TMS. Ascend through the lower Dhauladhar grassland and forest past the Rawa shepherd hamlet. Bonthu is a small seasonal Gaddi settlement — basic overnight possible in a shepherd shelter or self-tent.

itinerary.title: Bonthu → Bagga High Camp
itinerary.desc: Above Bonthu the trail enters the upper Dhauladhar meadows. Bagga is the last shepherd camp before the pass — a wide grassy shelf with Kangra Valley views far below and the Gag Pass headwall above.

itinerary.title: Bagga → Gaj Pass (4,164m) → Lamdal
itinerary.camp: Lam Dal Lake camp (3,900m) — self tent
itinerary.desc: Ascend to Gag Pass through rocky terrain. The pass commands views of the Kangra Valley behind and the wild Lam Dal Lake zone ahead. Steep descent into the Lamdal forest — one of the most isolated areas in the Dhauladhar.

itinerary.title: Lamdal → Return to road → Dharamshala
itinerary.desc: Trek out from Lamdal through forest to the nearest road. Drive back to Dharamshala. Per HP TMS the standard itinerary is 'Rawa–Bagga night stay–Lamdal stay and back.'

coverImageCredit: Photo by Chandi Saha on Pexels

name: Nohradhar–Churdhar Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration + Sirmaur DFO Forest Permit
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Nohradhar check-post, Sirmaur district
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Sirmaur DFO forest permit; Churdhar temple: free
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 75). Nohradhar is in Sirmaur district, reachable from Rajgarh. The HP TMS classifies this approach as HARD due to steeper terrain than the standard Nauradhar route. Nearest hospital: Regional Hospital Nahan (01702-222406). Shirgul Maharaj temple at summit is an active Hindu shrine open year-round. Wind-chill at the summit ridge can be severe — carry extra warm layers.

description: The harder, wilder approach to Churdhar Peak (3,647m) from Nohradhar in Sirmaur district — classified HARD by the HP government TMS (ID 75). While the standard Nauradhar approach is a well-worn pilgrim path, the Nohradhar route is steeper, more remote, and sees far fewer visitors. The same sacred Shirgul Maharaj temple crowns the summit — the protector deity of Sirmaur — with its extraordinary 360° panorama from the Punjab plains to the Greater Himalayan peaks.

overview.location: Churdhar (3,647m) is the highest summit of the outer Himalayan Churdhardhar range, Sirmaur district. The Nohradhar approach starts from Nohradhar village in Sirmaur, ascending more steeply and directly than the well-known Nauradhar route. The summit Shirgul Maharaj temple is the most important deity shrine across a wide swath of Sirmaur and Shimla hill communities.
overview.history: Shirgul Maharaj (also called Churdhar Maharaj) is the presiding deity of the outer Himachal hills — his temple at the summit receives pilgrims from the Nohradhar direction as well as the Nauradhar approach. The HP government distinguished these two routes in the TMS: Nauradhar is registered as MEDIUM (ID 80 — 'Deedag–Churdhar'), Nohradhar as HARD (ID 75 — 'Nohradhar–Churdhar Trek'), reflecting the more demanding terrain.
overview.length: 24 km round-trip from Nohradhar. Elevation gain from Nohradhar (approximately 1,900m) to summit (3,647m): 1,755m — steeper than the Nauradhar approach. Day 1: Nohradhar to forest camp (3,000m). Day 2: Forest camp to summit and return to Nohradhar.
overview.temperature: Apr–May: 5°C–18°C; rhododendron bloom spectacular. Sep–Oct: 0°C–15°C; clearest views. Summit is extremely exposed to wind — wind-chill can plunge severely even in October. Nov–Mar: Snow blocks the summit ridge.
overview.fitness: Hard. Steeper gradient and longer elevation gain than the Nauradhar route. Prior experience on multi-day high-altitude walks essential. Exposed summit ridge requires good weather assessment. Preparation: 8–10 weeks intensive training.

itinerary.title: Nohradhar → Forest Camp
itinerary.desc: Register TMS at Nohradhar. The trail is steep from the start through exceptional mixed Himalayan forest — oak, rhododendron, deodar. Excellent bird habitat: Himalayan monal, Koklas pheasant. Camp at forest rest house near treeline.

itinerary.title: Forest Camp → Churdhar Summit → Return to Nohradhar
itinerary.desc: Early start for the exposed summit ridge. Shirgul Maharaj temple at the top. The panorama from 3,647m: Punjab/Haryana plains visible 200 km south; Greater Himalayan peaks including Swargarohini and Bandarpoonch to the north. Return via the same steep path — trekking poles essential for the knee-testing descent.

coverImageCredit: Photo by ASHISH SHARMA on Pexels

name: Deedag–Churdhar Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration + Sirmaur DFO Forest Permit
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Deedag/Sangrah area check-post, Sirmaur district
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Sirmaur DFO forest permit
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 80). A third officially registered approach to Churdhar Peak (3,647m) from the Deedag side of Sirmaur district — classified HARD per HP TMS. The Deedag route is the least-known of the three government-registered Churdhar approaches (Nohradhar HARD ID75, Deedag HARD ID80, and the Nauradhar/Habban–Banalidhar route). Nearest hospital: CHC Sangrah (01702-248191). Police Sangrah: 01702-248201. HPPWD Rest House available.

coverImageCredit: Photo by RealHimachal on Brave Search
description: A third officially registered approach to the sacred Churdhar Peak (3,647m) — this time from the Deedag side of Sirmaur district, classified HARD by the HP TMS (ID 80). The Deedag–Churdhar route is the most remote and least-visited of the three government-registered approaches to the Shirgul Maharaj summit temple. The route traverses the wild outer Himalayan ridges of Sirmaur, passing through forest zones of extraordinary biodiversity on the way to the same spectacular summit with its plains-to-peaks 360° view.

overview.location: The Deedag approach to Churdhar (3,647m) starts from Deedag village in Sirmaur district near Sangrah — the same sub-district as the Habban–Banalidhar approach. Sangrah is 25–30 km from Nahan (Sirmaur HQ). The HP TMS lists Sangrah area infrastructure for this route including CHC Sangrah hospital and Sangrah Police Station.
overview.history: The Deedag route is one of the traditional approaches to Churdhar used by Sirmaur communities in this part of the district. It represents a lesser-known pilgrimage path to the Shirgul Maharaj shrine. The HP government added all three Churdhar routes (Nohradhar, Deedag, Habban–Banalidhar) to the TMS as HARD treks to capture the full complexity of approaches to this important religious summit.
overview.length: 28 km over 3 days from Deedag. Total elevation gain from Deedag village to summit (3,647m) approximately 1,800m. The specific campsite and route details match the Sangrah district infrastructure.
overview.temperature: Same as all Churdhar approaches. Best Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov. Summit very exposed to wind — prepare for extreme wind-chill at the top.
overview.fitness: Hard. Remote route with limited infrastructure. Full camping self-sufficiency required. Prior multi-day trekking experience essential. The HP TMS classifies this as HARD.

itinerary.title: Nahan/Sangrah → Deedag → Forest Camp
itinerary.camp: Forest camp (2,700m) — HPPWD or self tent
itinerary.desc: Drive from Nahan or Sangrah to Deedag trailhead. Register TMS. Ascend through Sirmaur's distinctive outer Himalayan mixed forest. The forest biodiversity on this approach is outstanding — large undisturbed woodland with pheasant and deer.

itinerary.title: Forest Camp → Ridge approach → Churdhar Summit
itinerary.desc: Climb through the upper forest and onto the open Churdhardhar ridge. Shirgul Maharaj temple at the summit. The same extraordinary 360° panorama: plains and peaks simultaneously visible. Descend to mid-camp or camp near summit for next day's return.

itinerary.title: Return to Deedag → Sangrah
itinerary.desc: Morning descent through the forest back to Deedag. Drive from Deedag to Sangrah or Nahan for onward travel.

coverImageCredit: Photo by RealHimachal on Brave Search

name: Habban–Banalidhar–Churdhar Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration + Sirmaur DFO Forest Permit
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Habban area check-post, Sirmaur district
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Sirmaur DFO forest permit
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 79). The longest and most remote of the three Churdhar approaches. Habban is in Sirmaur district. The Banalidhar ridge section is remote with unmarked trail — a local guide is strongly recommended. Full camping self-sufficiency required beyond Habban. The HP TMS classifies this as HARD.

coverImageCredit: Photo by DigiBrar on Pexels
description: The longest and most demanding of the three HP government–registered routes to Churdhar Peak (3,647m) — classified HARD (trek ID 79). The Habban–Banalidhar approach traverses the most remote section of the Churdhardhar range in Sirmaur district, offering superb solitude through extensive old-growth forest before joining the main ridge to the Shirgul Maharaj summit temple. Wildlife is abundant in this least-disturbed Churdhar approach: Himalayan monal, deer, possibly brown bear.

overview.location: The Habban–Banalidhar route approaches Churdhar from the west through Habban village in Sirmaur district. The Banalidhar section is a long forested ridge that connects Habban with the main Churdhardhar crest. Habban is reachable from Rajgarh (Sirmaur) — the key administrative centre for this part of the outer Himachal hills.
overview.history: The Habban area has been part of the traditional pilgrimage network to Churdhar for centuries, with local communities in western Sirmaur using this approach. The HP government distinguished this as a separate HARD route (ID 79) in the TMS, recognising its significantly longer distance and more demanding terrain compared to the Nauradhar approach. The Banalidhar ridge is one of the most wildlife-rich sections of the outer Himalayan forest in HP.
overview.length: 36 km over 3–4 days. Habban to Banalidhar base: 12 km. Banalidhar ridge section to upper camp: 10 km. Upper camp to summit and return: 14 km. Total elevation gain from Habban (approximately 1,800m) to summit (3,647m): approximately 1,855m.
overview.temperature: Same as all Churdhar routes. Best Apr–Jun and Sep–Nov. Banalidhar ridge is very exposed — prepare for wind.
overview.fitness: Hard. The longest approach to Churdhar with the most remote terrain. Good multi-day hiking fitness and full self-sufficiency required. A local guide for the Banalidhar section is strongly recommended for route navigation.

itinerary.title: Rajgarh/Sangrah → Habban → Banalidhar base
itinerary.desc: Drive to Habban. Register TMS. The trail immediately enters exceptional outer Himalayan forest — one of the finest sections of undisturbed old-growth woodland in Sirmaur. Bird and wildlife watching outstanding throughout.

itinerary.title: Banalidhar base → Banalidhar ridge → Upper camp
itinerary.desc: The Banalidhar ridge itself — wide and forested, with expanding views of the Sirmaur valleys. The trail narrows toward the main Churdhardhar crest. Navigation requires a guide in sections where the path is unclear.

itinerary.title: Upper camp → Churdhar Summit → Return descent
itinerary.desc: Summit day. Shirgul Maharaj temple at Churdhar. The complete plains-to-peaks panorama from one of Himachal's most isolated summit approaches — all the more rewarding for the remote journey here.

coverImageCredit: Photo by Digibrar on Digibrar

name: Bawa Pass Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration + Kinnaur ILP (foreigners) + Forest Permit
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Bhawanagar check-post, Kinnaur; Guide: Tourism Information Center Reckong Peo (01786-222253)
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Kinnaur Protected Area Permit for foreigners from SDM Recong Peo; Forest/Rest House: 01786-8219120140
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 93). Open 15 Jun–15 Sep per HP TMS (7 days minimum). Classified EASY by HP TMS despite the 4,890m altitude — reflecting the gradual approach rather than technical difficulty. Police Bhawanagar: 01786-263455. Bus Stand Bhawanagar is the nearest transit hub. Landmarks: Bhawanagar and Tapri. Forest and HPPWD Rest Houses available en route. Foreigners require Inner Line Permit from SDM Recong Peo.

description: A 7-day trek to the impressive Bawa Pass (4,890m) in Kinnaur district — one of the highest officially registered 'easy' treks in the HP government TMS (ID 93), reflecting its gradual approach rather than technical difficulty. The route passes through the spectacular Kinnaur landscape of deep gorges, ancient villages, apple orchards, and dramatic Himalayan scenery on the approach from Bhawanagar to the high pass above Tapri. The extraordinarily deep Sutlej gorge below is visible throughout the approach.

overview.location: Bawa Pass (4,890m) is in Kinnaur district, in the high ranges above the Sutlej River gorge. The HP TMS lists Bhawanagar (31.787°N, 77.996°E) as the base camp and Tapri as the second landmark. Bhawanagar and Tapri are both accessible from Recong Peo, the Kinnaur district headquarters.
overview.history: Kinnauri communities have used the high passes of this region for inter-village communication and seasonal herding for centuries. The HP government registered Bawa Pass (trek ID 93) despite its modest TMS classification — the high altitude and remote Kinnaur context make this a serious undertaking. The Tourism Information Center in Recong Peo coordinates guides and assists with permit processing for this route.
overview.length: 55 km over 7 days per HP TMS (minimum 7 days). Elevation gain from Bhawanagar to Bawa Pass (4,890m): approximately 2,500m. Forest and HPPWD Rest Houses provide accommodation at key points along the route.
overview.temperature: Jun: 0°C–18°C; snow still on pass approaches. Jul–Aug: 5°C–22°C; best season; green and spectacular. Sep: 0°C–15°C; stable and clear; recommended. Outside Jun–Sep: Pass blocked per HP TMS.
overview.fitness: Moderate–Hard (despite HP TMS 'Easy' classification). The 4,890m pass altitude and 7-day duration demand sustained fitness and acclimatisation. The 'easy' designation reflects gradual gradient rather than low effort. Prior multi-day high-altitude experience recommended.

itinerary.title: Recong Peo → Bhawanagar (base camp)
itinerary.desc: Drive from Recong Peo to Bhawanagar via Tapri. Register TMS and collect guide from Tourism Information Center R-Peo (01786-222253). Bhawanagar is on the deep Sutlej gorge — extraordinary views of the granite canyon walls.

itinerary.title: Bhawanagar → Valley ascent Day 1
itinerary.desc: Begin ascending from Bhawanagar through the characteristic Kinnauri landscape — terraced fields, ancient stone villages, and the progressive narrowing of the valley above.

itinerary.title: Valley Day 2 → High meadow camp
itinerary.desc: Above the village zone into the high meadow and pastoral zone. The Kinnaur Himalayan peaks begin to dominate the skyline. Acclimatisation critical at this altitude.

itinerary.title: High meadow → Bawa Pass approach
itinerary.desc: Approach the pass base through increasingly rocky high-alpine terrain. The full sweep of the Kinnaur Himalaya is visible.

itinerary.title: Bawa Pass (4,890m) — Summit and return to high meadow
itinerary.desc: Cross the Bawa Pass at 4,890m — extraordinary Kinnaur high-altitude panorama. The deep Sutlej gorge, Kinnaur Kailash (6,050m), and the Tibetan plateau beyond the border are visible. Descend to high meadow.

itinerary.title: High meadow → Bhawanagar descent
itinerary.desc: Long return descent to Bhawanagar through the valley and village zones.

itinerary.title: Bhawanagar → Recong Peo → Departure
itinerary.camp: Return to Recong Peo or Shimla
itinerary.desc: Drive from Bhawanagar back to Recong Peo. Depart for Shimla (235 km, 7 hrs) or Manali via Wangtu–Rampur.

coverImageCredit: Photo by UTkarsh on Pexels

name: Bhangayini Mata Temple to Fort Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Haripurdhar bus stop, Sirmaur district
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Trekker's Hostel Himachal Tourism: 9736000034; HPPWD Rest House: 01702-248207
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 84). Open 17 Jun–31 Dec per HP TMS. HP TMS itinerary: 'Haripurdhar to Trekker's Hostel Forest Rest House (Old Fort).' CHC Sangrah hospital: 01702-248191. Police Sangrah: 01702-248201. The HP TMS describes Haripurdhar as 'a beautiful village and upcoming tourist destination especially for spiritual, leisure, nature tourism — famous for Maa Bhangayini Temple.' Arya Petrol Pump at Kakog is the nearest fuel station.

description: A spiritual and scenic day trek in the Haripurdhar area of Sirmaur district — from the sacred Maa Bhangayini Mata Temple to the old Forest Rest House (ancient fort site) at 2,500m. Registered on the HP government TMS (ID 84) as an easy 1-day route. Haripurdhar is described by the HP TMS as 'an upcoming tourist destination for spiritual, leisure, and nature tourism.' The trek combines religious heritage with forest walking and views of the Sirmaur hills.

overview.location: The trek runs through Haripurdhar village in Sirmaur district, starting at the Bhangayini Mata Temple and reaching the Trekker's Hostel / Old Fort Forest Rest House (2,500m). Haripurdhar is 25 km from Sangrah, 60 km from Nahan. The HP TMS notes the Arya Petrol Pump at Kakog as the nearest fuel and HPPWD Rest House (01702-248207) and the Trekker's Hostel Himachal Tourism (9736000034) as accommodation options.
overview.history: Bhangayini Mata (Maa Bhangayini) is a significant goddess in the Sirmaur district's religious landscape. The Haripurdhar area has been a pilgrimage destination for communities throughout southern Himachal Pradesh. The old fort (now a Forest Rest House) at the end of the trek represents the military history of the outer Himachal hills — the Rajput kingdoms of Sirmaur maintained fortified positions on these ridges for centuries.
overview.length: 8 km one-way (Haripurdhar to Forest Rest House/Fort), approximately 16 km round-trip or one-way with vehicle return. Elevation gain from Haripurdhar to 2,500m FRH.
overview.temperature: Open 17 Jun–31 Dec per HP TMS. Jun–Aug: 15°C–28°C; monsoon green and pleasant. Sep–Nov: 8°C–22°C; clear skies; excellent views. Dec: 2°C–12°C; cool and atmospheric.
overview.fitness: Easy. A short spiritual walk through forest on a well-used trail. Suitable for pilgrims, families, and all levels of fitness. Trekker's Hostel Himachal Tourism at the destination provides accommodation.

itinerary.title: Haripurdhar → Bhangayini Mata Temple → Old Fort (FRH)
itinerary.camp: Trekker's Hostel (9736000034) or return same day
itinerary.desc: Begin at Haripurdhar bus stop and visit the Maa Bhangayini Temple. Register TMS. The forest walk to the old fort / Trekker's Hostel passes through pine and oak — the Sirmaur hills are visible across the valleys. The Trekker's Hostel offers overnight accommodation in a heritage forest rest house setting.

coverImageCredit: Photo by Raj Manohar on Pexels

name: Banethi–Jamta Nature Trail

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration
permitInfo.where: Online at trekking.hp.gov.in; Banethi Forest Rest House starting point
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory free registration; Banethi FRH: 01702-222240; Grand View Resort Jamta: 9418148267; Sirmaur Retreat Resort: 8988241648
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 115). Open 17 Jun–31 Dec per HP TMS. The HP TMS gives the most detailed description of any of its registered treks: '7 km Banethi to Jamta trek starts from beautiful Forest Rest House at Banethi built in 1905 of sandstone and wood in old architectural style. Beautiful Pine Forest, breezy and tranquil landscapes, small happy villages, birds flocking and chirping. Leads to famous leisure tourist spot Jamta overlooking Nahan Town and vast plains on one side and Churdhar range on the other.' Hospital Dr. Y.S. Parmar Medical College, Nahan: 01702-222209. Police Nahan: 01702-522522.

description: A beautiful 7 km forest nature trail from the historic Banethi Forest Rest House (built 1905) to the leisure spot of Jamta — one of the most evocatively described treks in the HP government's official TMS (ID 115). The trail passes through 'beautiful Pine Forest, breezy and tranquil landscapes, small happy villages, birds flocking and chirping' with Jamta overlooking both Nahan town and the vast Punjab plains on one side, and the Churdhar range on the other. A perfect half-day walk near Nahan.

overview.location: The trail runs from Banethi village (on NH907A) through Nauni village to Jamta — three settlements described in detail in the HP TMS. Banethi is the starting point with its landmark 1905 sandstone-and-wood Forest Rest House. Jamta is approximately 10 km from Nahan, near Renuka Ji — 'an upcoming tourist destination especially for leisure, rural and nature-based tourism with luxury resorts.'
overview.history: The Banethi Forest Rest House was built in 1905 in the old colonial architectural style — one of the few surviving examples of British-era forest department architecture in Sirmaur. Jamta's position overlooking both the Nahan valley and the great sweep of the Punjab plains made it an important vantage point. The HP TMS gives this trail an unusually detailed and poetic description, making it stand out among the otherwise sparse HP government trek records.
overview.length: 7 km one-way, Banethi to Jamta (14 km round-trip or one-way with vehicle return from Jamta to Banethi). Per HP TMS itinerary: 'Banethi to Jamta Eco Trail — 7 km' / 'Banethi–Nauni–Jamta 7km.'
overview.temperature: Open year-round per HP TMS (1 Jun–31 Dec). Oct–Feb: 5°C–18°C; clearest views of Churdhar range and plains. Mar–Jun: 10°C–30°C; spring flowers and birdsong. Jul–Sep: 15°C–28°C; lush and verdant; birds at peak activity.
overview.fitness: Easy. A 7 km forest nature walk at low altitude (1,350m). Suitable for all ages, families, and casual walkers. One of the most accessible treks on the HP TMS. Luxury resort accommodation available at Jamta destination.

itinerary.title: Banethi Forest Rest House → Nauni → Jamta
itinerary.camp: Day trek — Grand View Resort Jamta (9418148267) or Sirmaur Retreat (8988241648) for overnight option
itinerary.desc: Start from the 1905 Banethi Forest Rest House (01702-222240) — the sandstone-and-wood colonial building is a landmark worth exploring before the walk. The pine forest path to Nauni and Jamta is 'breezy and tranquil' per HP TMS. Jamta's dual outlook — Nahan town and plains behind, Churdhar range ahead — is the scenic payoff of this short but rewarding nature trail.

coverImageCredit: Photo by Alwick Gadgets on Pexels

name: Lamkhaga Pass Trek (Chhitkul–Harshil)

permitInfo.type: HP TMS + Kinnaur ILP (foreigners) + Uttarakhand Forest/Gangotri area permit
permitInfo.where: HP TMS: trekking.hp.gov.in; Kinnaur PAP: SDM Recong Peo (foreigners); Uttarakhand: Uttarkashi DFO (Harshil/Gangotri side)
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory; Kinnaur ILP for foreigners from SDM R-Peo; Uttarakhand Gangotri buffer zone permit at Harshil
permitInfo.note: HP TMS mandatory (trek ID 88). Open Jun–Sep per HP TMS; operators also run May and Oct seasons when conditions allow. This is a rare HP-Uttarakhand crossover trek starting from Chhitkul (Kinnaur, HP) and ending at Harshil in the Gangotri valley (Uttarakhand). 5,282m pass crossing — serious high-altitude expedition. Guide from Tourism Information Center Reckong Peo (01786-222253). PHC Chitkul: 01786-242278. Forest & HPPWD Rest Houses en route. Police Chowki Sangla: 01786-222270. Bus Stand Sangla is the nearest transit hub.

description: The Lamkhaga Pass (5,282m) trek — one of the most challenging crossover expeditions in the Indian Himalayas, connecting Chhitkul (the last village on the old Hindustan-Tibet Road in Kinnaur, HP) with Harshil in the Gangotri valley (Uttarakhand). First crossed by Greek-British mountaineer Marco Pallis in 1933. Registered as HARD on the HP government TMS (ID 88). The crossing traverses the Baspa–Gangotri watershed through one of the most remote and scenically overwhelming landscapes in the western Himalayas — linking the Tibetan-Buddhist culture of Kinnaur with the Hindu pilgrimage tradition of the Gangotri valley.

overview.location: Chhitkul (3,450m) is the last permanently inhabited village on the old Hindustan-Tibet Road, Baspa Valley, Kinnaur. Harshil (2,620m) is a village in the Bhagirathi River valley, Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand — 24 km from the Gangotri glacier. The trek crosses the Baspa–Bhagirathi watershed at approximately 5,400m. The HP TMS lists this as '80 KM Trek (one side)' with a Chitkul to Gangotri Trek landmark.
overview.history: The Baspa–Gangotri watershed crossing is one of the legendary trans-Himalayan routes of the western Himalayas, used historically by traders and pilgrims moving between the Kinnaur highlands and the Gangotri pilgrimage circuit. Chhitkul's ancient temples and the last-village atmosphere make it one of Kinnaur's most atmospheric trekking bases. Harshil is the gateway to Gangotri and one of the most beautiful villages in the Bhagirathi Valley.
overview.length: 70 km over 7 days per HP TMS (minimum 7 days). The pass crossing at 5,400m is the crux. One-way from Chhitkul to Harshil requires transport logistics at both ends — Sangla on the HP side, Harshil/Uttarkashi on the Uttarakhand side.
overview.temperature: Jul: 0°C–15°C; glacier accessible with crampons. Aug: Most stable; peak season. Sep: –5°C to 12°C; clearest skies. Outside Jul–Sep: Pass inaccessible per HP TMS.
overview.fitness: Expert. A 5,282m pass crossing with glacier travel in a completely remote wilderness. Prior expedition experience essential. Guide from Tourism Information Center Recong Peo is mandatory per HP TMS.

itinerary.title: Shimla/R-Peo → Sangla → Chhitkul
itinerary.desc: Drive from Shimla via Rampur and the deep Sutlej gorge to Sangla and Chhitkul. Collect guide from Tourism Information Center Recong Peo. Chhitkul — last village before China — is surrounded by apple orchards and ancient wooden temples. Acclimatise for one night.

itinerary.title: Chhitkul → Baspa upper valley
itinerary.desc: Ascend above Chhitkul along the Baspa River into the wilderness. The valley widens into moraine and glacial terrain above the village zone.

itinerary.title: Upper Baspa → Glacier base camp
itinerary.desc: Approach the Baspa–Gangotri watershed glacier. The guide identifies the safe route through crevasse zones. Crampons required from here.

itinerary.title: Pass crossing (5,400m) → Descent to Uttarakhand side
itinerary.desc: Alpine start at 4 AM. The 5,282m pass is the highest point of the expedition. Long descent on the Gangotri side into increasingly vegetated terrain.

itinerary.title: Uttarakhand valley → Harshil approach
itinerary.desc: Descend through the dramatic Bhagirathi upper reaches toward Harshil. The transition from barren Kinnaur landscape to the forested Uttarakhand valleys is extraordinary.

itinerary.title: Harshil → Uttarkashi → Departure
itinerary.desc: Drive from Harshil to Uttarkashi and onwards. The Gangotri highway through the Bhagirathi gorge is magnificent. From Uttarkashi: buses and taxis to Rishikesh (182 km, 6 hrs) or Delhi (480 km).

coverImageCredit: Photo by UTkarsh on Pexels

name: Vasuki Tal Trek (Gangotri–Nandanvan)

permitInfo.type: Gangotri National Park Permit + Uttarkashi DFO Camping Permit
permitInfo.where: Gangotri National Park permit at Gangotri entry gate; camping fees at Bhojbasa, Tapovan, Nandanvan checkposts
permitInfo.fee: Gangotri National Park entry fee; camping fee per night at regulated campsites; guide recommended (highly advised for glacier crossings)
permitInfo.note: This is an entirely different lake from Vasuki Tal near Kedarnath (Trek ID 410). This Vasuki Tal (4,880m) is in Uttarkashi district, Gangotri National Park. Route involves two serious glacier crossings — the Gangotri Glacier (Gomukh to Nandanvan) and the Chaturangi Glacier (Nandanvan to Vasuki Tal). Crampons and trekking poles essential. A guide experienced in glacier crossings is strongly recommended. Network available only in Gangotri — carry power banks. Last electricity at Gangotri. Best approached with prior high-altitude experience above 4,000m.

description: A demanding 9–10 day expedition into the heart of the Gangotri National Park reaching Vasuki Tal (4,880m) — a sacred glacial lake at the base of Mt. Vasuki Parbat (6,792m) and Mt. Satopanth (7,075m). Not to be confused with Vasuki Tal (4,135m) near Kedarnath — this is an entirely different, higher, and more remote lake in Uttarkashi district. The route passes through Gaumukh (source of the Ganga), the legendary Tapovan meadow beneath Shivling (6,543m), two major glacier crossings, and Nandanvan meadow (4,340m) before the Chaturangi Glacier approach to the lake. One of the most spectacular wilderness treks in India.

overview.location: This Vasuki Tal (4,880m) is in Uttarkashi district, Gangotri National Park — 7 km from Nandanvan meadow (4,340m) via the Chaturangi Glacier. It serves as the base camp for Mt. Satopanth (7,075m) and Mt. Vasuki Parbat (6,792m). The complete route from Gangotri (3,048m): Gangotri → Chirbasa (3,600m) → Bhojbasa (3,792m) → Gaumukh (3,890m, source of the Ganga) → Tapovan (4,463m) → Nandanvan (4,340m) → Vasuki Tal (4,880m). Total: ~65 km round trip. This is a completely different lake from Vasuki Tal (4,135m) near Kedarnath (Trek ID 410), which is in Rudraprayag district.
overview.history: Gaumukh — passed en route — is the glacial snout from which the sacred Bhagirathi River (upper Ganga) emerges, one of the holiest sites in Hinduism. Tapovan is a legendary alpine meadow where sadhus have meditated for centuries beneath the north face of Shivling. Nandanvan is the base camp for expeditions to Bhagirathi I, II, III peaks. Vasuki Tal itself is named for Vasuki — the serpent of Lord Shiva — and, like its Kedarnath namesake, is associated with Raksha Bandhan mythology. The Gangotri Glacier is one of the largest in the Himalaya; scientific monitoring stations track its rapid retreat due to climate change.
overview.length: 65 km round trip over 9–10 days. Key segments: Gangotri→Bhojbasa (14 km, Day 1); Bhojbasa→Gaumukh→Tapovan (9 km, Day 2); rest/acclimatisation at Tapovan (Day 3); Tapovan→Nandanvan via Gangotri Glacier (6–7 km, Day 4); Nandanvan→Vasuki Tal→Nandanvan via Chaturangi Glacier (12 km round trip, Day 5–6); Nandanvan→Bhojbasa (14 km, Day 7); Bhojbasa→Gangotri (14 km, Day 8); drive Gangotri→Dehradun (258 km, Day 9).
overview.temperature: May–Jun: 0°C–15°C at Tapovan; –10°C at Vasuki Tal overnight; heavy snow possible at the lake in May. Sep–Oct: –5°C to 12°C at Tapovan; –15°C at Vasuki Tal overnight; clearest skies and most stable weather — recommended season. Jul–Aug: Partial monsoon rain; glacier more dangerous; not recommended. Nov–Apr: National Park closed; inaccessible.
overview.fitness: Hard. Two serious glacier crossings with crevasse risk require good balance, stamina, and ideally previous glacier experience. The 4,880m altitude demands thorough acclimatisation at Tapovan and Nandanvan before the lake push. Prior multi-day high-altitude Himalayan trek experience (above 4,000m) is mandatory. Preparation: 10–12 weeks of intensive cardio and loaded hiking.

itinerary.title: Dehradun/Rishikesh → Uttarkashi → Gangotri
itinerary.desc: Drive to Gangotri (3,048m / 10,000 ft) in Uttarkashi district. Collect Gangotri National Park permit at the entry gate. Visit the Gangotri temple — one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites. Evening acclimatisation walk along the Bhagirathi.

itinerary.title: Gangotri → Chirbasa → Bhojbasa
itinerary.desc: Trek along the Bhagirathi River through pine and bhojpatra (birch) forest to Chirbasa (3,600m, tree line), then through increasingly barren terrain to Bhojbasa. Spectacular sunset views of the Bhagirathi group of peaks.

itinerary.title: Bhojbasa → Gaumukh → Tapovan
itinerary.desc: Early morning panorama of Bhagirathi peaks from Bhojbasa. Trek to Gaumukh (3,890m) — the glacial snout where the sacred Bhagirathi emerges from ice. Then a steep ascent up the moraine and rocky face to Tapovan — one of the finest alpine meadows in the Himalaya, directly beneath the vertical north face of Shivling (6,543m).

itinerary.title: Tapovan — Acclimatisation + Exploration
itinerary.desc: Rest and acclimatise at Tapovan. Optional excursion to Neel Tal and Shivling base camp (4,619m) for acclimatisation. Tapovan is base camp for multiple Himalayan peaks — expeditions to Shivling, Meru, Bhagirathi peaks are visible. Astrophotography and Milky Way views at night are extraordinary here.

itinerary.title: Tapovan → Gangotri Glacier crossing → Nandanvan
itinerary.desc: The most technically demanding day. Descend from Tapovan onto the Gangotri Glacier — a wide moraine-covered glacier with crevasses. Cross carefully with guide. Ascend to Nandanvan — a high meadow at 4,340m that is the base camp for Bhagirathi I, II, III expeditions. Views of Vasuki Parbat and Satopanth now dominate the skyline.

itinerary.title: Nandanvan → Chaturangi Glacier → Vasuki Tal → Nandanvan
itinerary.desc: Start early. The trail follows the right side of the Chaturangi Glacier toward Vasuki Tal — a steady upward traverse. The lake at 4,880m is a small but breathtaking high-altitude tarn at the base of Satopanth (7,075m) and Vasuki Parbat (6,792m). Spend time at the lake, then retrace to Nandanvan.

itinerary.title: Nandanvan → Bhojbasa (via Gangotri Glacier return)
itinerary.desc: Retrace through Nandanvan and back across the Gangotri Glacier to Bhojbasa. The views looking back at the glacial wilderness are as dramatic on the return as on the approach.

itinerary.title: Bhojbasa → Gangotri
itinerary.desc: Final descent through the birch forest and along the Bhagirathi back to Gangotri. Visit the Gangotri temple aarti in the evening.

itinerary.title: Gangotri → Uttarkashi → Dehradun
itinerary.desc: Drive back from Gangotri to Dehradun through the Bhagirathi gorge, past Harsil, Uttarkashi, and Tehri Lake. The drive through the Himalayan valleys is spectacular.

coverImageCredit: Photo by INDU BIKASH SARKER on Pexels

name: Shrikhand Mahadev Yatra
distance: 35 km one way / 70 km round trip

permitInfo.type: Himachal Pradesh State Government — Shrikhand Yatra Registration
permitInfo.cost: Registration fee for official Yatra period: nominal (state government sets annual fee). Forest entry fees apply. Camping fees at official campsites.
permitInfo.process: During the official Yatra (July–August), trekkers must register with the HP government. Medical fitness certificate required. Identity proof mandatory. Outside the Yatra period, trek independently but inform local forest office at Nirmand. Register at checkpost in Jaon village.
permitInfo.foreigners: Open to all nationalities, though the trek is remote with limited emergency services. High physical fitness and prior mountain experience strongly recommended for foreign trekkers.
permitInfo.note: The Yatra period (July–August) is the only time campsites, langars (free food by Sikh/Hindu community organizations), and emergency support are available on the route. Outside the Yatra, the trail is completely unsupported. At least 3–5 deaths occur on this trek annually — the HP government has issued multiple warnings. This is not a trek for beginners under any circumstances.

startPoint: Jaon Village, Nirmand sub-division, Kullu, Himachal Pradesh
nearestRailhead: Shimla (170 km, narrow gauge from Kalka) / Chandigarh (250 km)
nearestAirport: Bhuntar Airport, Kullu (120 km from Jaon)
description: One of the toughest pilgrimage treks in India — a brutal, beautiful climb to a 75-foot natural Shivalingam at 5,227m (17,150 ft) in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh. One of the Panch Kailash (five sacred Kailash peaks of the Himalayas), this is a trek of extreme physical demand, glacial crossings, near-vertical sections called Bheem Ki Sidhis, and profound religious power. The annual Shrikhand Yatra draws tens of thousands of pilgrims each July–August.

overview.location: Shrikhand Mahadev (5,227m) is in the Nirmand sub-division of Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh. The trek begins from Jaon village (1,950m) on the right bank of the Kurpan stream, reached via Rampur–Nirmand from Shimla (approx. 140 km). The route climbs 3,277m of elevation over 32 km (one way) through Thaachru, Kali Ghati, Bheemdwar, Parvati Baag, and Nain Sarovar before the final ascent to the summit.
overview.history: Shrikhand Mahadev is one of the Panch Kailash — the five peaks in the Indian Himalayas considered abodes of Lord Shiva, alongside Kailash Mansarovar, Adi Kailash, Kinnaur Kailash, and Manimahesh Kailash. The 75-foot Shivalingam on the summit is a natural rock formation. Legend tells of the demon Bhasmasura, who obtained from Shiva the boon that anyone he touched would turn to ash — then turned it on Shiva himself. Lord Vishnu saved Shiva in the guise of Mohini; the demon's blood turned the soil here red. The Himachal Pradesh government organizes the official Shrikhand Yatra from Ashada Poornima to Shravana Poornima (full moon to full moon, July–August) each year.
overview.length: 65 km round trip from Jaon. Elevation gain of approximately 3,277m one way — among the steepest elevation gains of any pilgrimage trek in India. The final 6 km from Parvati Baag to the summit involves glacier crossings and near-vertical rock scrambles.
overview.temperature: At summit (5,227m): well below 0°C even in July–August. At Thaachru (3,450m): 5–15°C days in season. Snow is present above Kali Ghati year-round. Sudden storms and whiteout conditions are common and have caused fatalities.
overview.fitness: Hard to Very Hard. Considered one of the most demanding treks in India. Steep elevation gain, high altitude (5,227m), glacier crossings, near-vertical rock scrambles (Bheem Ki Sidhis), and unpredictable weather. Only for experienced trekkers with prior high-altitude experience and excellent physical condition. Medical fitness check recommended.

itinerary.title: Shimla / Chandigarh to Jaon Village
itinerary.distance: 170 km from Shimla via Narkanda and Rampur (50 km Rampur to Jaon via Nirmand)
itinerary.desc: Drive from Shimla (170 km, 8-9 hrs) or Chandigarh (250 km, 9-10 hrs) via Narkanda, Rampur Bushahr. From Rampur, take a local bus or taxi via Nirmand to Jaon village (50 km, 3 hrs). Jaon (1,950m / 6,397 ft) is a small village of ~50 houses on the right bank of the Kurpan stream (which originates at Shrikhand). Beautiful apple orchards and direct views of the Shrikhand mountain range above. Guesthouses and homestays available. Register here for the yatra (HP government requires registration). Trek is ONLY open for 10-15 days per year (official dates released by HP government every July). Load up on supplies — limited food availability beyond Thachru.

itinerary.title: Jaon to Singhad — Trek to Thachru
itinerary.distance: 3-4 km Jaon to Singhad + 8 km Singhad to Thachru = ~11-12 km
itinerary.desc: Trek starts from Jaon. 3-4 km level trek along Kurpan stream to Singhad (2,095m / 6,873 ft) — last inhabited village, 1 hour. Temples and shrines at Singhad (pilgrims offer prayers here for safe return). Then 8 km steep ascent from Singhad to Thachru (3,450m) via Barahati Nala (stream crossing) — total 7-8 hrs from Jaon. Barahati Nala is the toughest section. The JustWravel trekker (2017 firsthand): Day 1 Jaon to Thachru ~11 km total. Thachru is the first major camp with tents, langars (free food by volunteers), and basic medical facilities. Stunning Himalayan views begin here.

itinerary.title: Thachru to Bheem Dwar via Kunsha
itinerary.distance: 7 km Thachru to Kunsha + 3.5 km Kunsha to Bheem Dwar = 10.5 km
itinerary.camp: Bheem Dwar — caves / tents (natural shelter under massive boulders)
itinerary.desc: 7 km from Thachru to Kunsha (12,500 ft) via Kali Ghati (steep ascent) and Bhimatalai (descent) — route as documented on OFFICIAL HP GOVT website. Kunsha is surrounded by multiple cascading waterfalls, 3-4 hrs from Thachru. Then 3.5 km further to Bheem Dwar (12,175 ft, 2-3 hrs). Bheem Dwar is a large bugyal (meadow) with massive boulders — Pandavas (specifically Bheem) are believed to have rested here during the Mahabharata exile. Ancient Bheem Lipi inscriptions on rocks. Natural cave shelters. Beyond here glaciers appear. Carry sufficient water from Bheem Dwar's streams.

itinerary.title: Bheem Dwar to Parvati Bagh — Acclimatisation
itinerary.distance: 3 km Bheem Dwar to Parvati Bagh
itinerary.camp: Parvati Bagh — tents (last campsite before summit)
itinerary.desc: 3 km from Bheem Dwar to Parvati Bagh (13,622 ft) — cross the largest waterfall on the trek en route. Parvati Bagh is a spectacular high-altitude meadow (home to Brahmakamal flowers, India's national flower) surrounded by glaciers and snow peaks. This is the last camp before the summit — stay here to acclimatise for the pre-dawn summit push tomorrow. Rest well, eat light, sleep early. Summit day requires a 3-4 AM start.

itinerary.title: Summit Day — Parvati Bagh to Shrikhand Mahadev Peak — Return to Bheem Dwar
itinerary.distance: Parvati Bagh to summit ~5-6 km one way via Nain Sarovar; return to Bheem Dwar ~8-9 km
itinerary.elevation: 5,227m / 17,150 ft (Shrikhand Mahadev — some sources cite 18,570 ft)
itinerary.camp: Bheem Dwar or Parvati Bagh (depending on conditions)
itinerary.desc: START 3-4 AM from Parvati Bagh. Trek ~2-3 km to Nain Sarovar (14,527 ft) — a frozen alpine lake where Goddess Parvati is said to have wept; take a holy dip (Brahmakamal flowers float here in season). From Nain Sarovar: extreme vertical climb through Bhim ki Bahi (15,921 ft), then final rocky vertical ascent (low oxygen, near zero degrees) to Shrikhand Mahadev peak. The 72-75 ft Shivling (Swayambhu, self-manifested) has eyes, nose, and matted hair visible in the rock — an awe-inspiring sight. DANGER: Many fatalities have occurred on this stretch. Do NOT proceed if weather turns bad. Descend carefully back to Parvati Bagh / Bheem Dwar. Trek open only 10-15 days/year — rescue teams stationed on route by HP government.

itinerary.title: Bheem Dwar to Thachru to Jaon — Return
itinerary.distance: 10.5 km Bheem Dwar to Thachru + 11-12 km Thachru to Jaon = ~22 km descent
itinerary.desc: Full descent day: Bheem Dwar → Thachru (10.5 km, 4-5 hrs) then Thachru → Jaon (11-12 km, 4-5 hrs) — knees and poles essential. Some strong trekkers combine the descent into 1 day (22 km). Reach Jaon by evening. Drive back to Shimla (170 km, 8-9 hrs) or halt overnight in Jaon / Rampur.

coverImageCredit: Photo by Bryanken on Pexels

name: Yulla Kanda Trek
description: A spiritually significant moderate trek in the remote Rora Valley of Kinnaur district, leading to a glacial lake at 3,895m beside which stands the world's highest Krishna temple — believed by locals to have been built by the Pandavas during their exile. The trek passes through dense pine and deodar forests, alpine meadows, and traditional Kinnauri villages. Far less known than Himachal's famous treks, Yulla Kanda offers complete solitude and extraordinary mountain views.

overview.location: Yulla Kanda (3,895m) is in the Rora Valley, Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh. The trek starts from Yulla Khas village (approx. 2,200m), reached from Tapri on the National Highway 5 (Hindustan–Tibet Road), which runs 190 km from Shimla to Reckong Peo. The glacial Yulla Kanda Lake beside the Krishna temple is the destination. The Kinnaur Kailash (6,050m) massif and the peaks of the greater Himalayan range dominate the eastern skyline throughout.
overview.history: The Yulla Kanda temple dedicated to Lord Krishna is considered the world's highest Krishna temple, at approximately 3,895m. Local Kinnauri tradition holds that the temple was constructed by the Pandavas during their 13-year exile in the Himalayas. The site gains special significance during Janmashtami (usually August–September), when hundreds of pilgrims and devotees gather at this extraordinary altitude to celebrate Lord Krishna's birth. The Kinnauri community has inhabited these remote Himalayan valleys for centuries, preserving a culture blending Hindu and Tibetan Buddhist traditions.
overview.length: 24 km round trip from Yulla Khas village. 12 km one way to the lake and temple. Elevation gain approximately 1,700m from the starting village. The trek can be completed in 2 trekking days plus travel days.
overview.temperature: June–September: 10–20°C days, 0–8°C nights at camp. October: dropping temperatures and possible early snow. Best in June–early October. The temple and trail are inaccessible October–May under snow.
overview.fitness: Easy to Moderate. The total distance and elevation gain are manageable for most healthy adults with reasonable fitness. Steep sections in the upper half. No technical terrain. Suitable for families and beginners with some walking experience.

permitInfo.type: Himachal Pradesh Forest Department — Kinnaur District
permitInfo.cost: No specific trekking permit fee reported as of 2025. Forest area entry fee may apply. Check with local forest office at Tapri or Reckong Peo.
permitInfo.process: No formal permit booking portal for this trek as of 2025. Register informally at the Yulla Khas village panchayat or local forest checkpost. Carry government-issued ID. Hiring a local guide from Yulla Khas is strongly recommended.
permitInfo.foreigners: Open to all nationalities. Kinnaur district is an Inner Line Permit (ILP) zone for sections near the Tibet border, but the Yulla Kanda trek itself does not require an ILP. Verify current requirements with Reckong Peo SDM office before traveling.
permitInfo.note: Mobile connectivity limited beyond Yulla Khas. Only BSNL, Jio, and Airtel may have intermittent signal. No medical facilities on the trail. Trail may be closed during heavy snowfall. Best visited during the Janmashtami festival for a unique cultural experience.

itinerary.title: Shimla to Yulla Khas via Tapri
itinerary.desc: Drive the spectacular Hindustan–Tibet Road from Shimla along the Satluj River gorge through Narkanda, Rampur, and the dramatic Wangtu bridge to Tapri. From Tapri, a rough mountain road climbs to the traditional Kinnauri village of Yulla Khas. The drive passes orchards of apple and apricot with the Kinnaur Kailash massif emerging on the eastern horizon. Overnight in a local homestay — experience authentic Kinnauri hospitality and food.

itinerary.title: Yulla Khas to Yulla Kanda Base Camp
itinerary.desc: The trail begins at the edge of Yulla Khas, climbing through dense pine and deodar forest before opening into expansive alpine meadows. The route follows a stream through wildflowers, with the first views of the snow peaks emerging as the trees thin. Reach a large meadow campsite ringed by the Himalayan skyline — an extraordinary setting for overnight camping under a canopy of stars.

itinerary.title: Base Camp to Yulla Kanda Lake and Return
itinerary.desc: Early start for the 4 km climb to Yulla Kanda Lake and the Krishna temple. The trail crosses moraines and boulder fields before the glacial lake appears — still and brilliant blue, ringed by the high peaks of the Kinnaur range. The small ancient stone temple on the lakeside, believed built by the Pandavas, is one of the most serene religious sites in the western Himalayas. During Janmashtami, the lake becomes a festival ground. Descend to base camp or all the way to Yulla Khas.

itinerary.title: Yulla Khas to Shimla / Chandigarh — Return Drive
itinerary.desc: Drive back along the Hindustan–Tibet Road through the Satluj gorge to Shimla, or continue to Chandigarh. The return journey through Rampur and Narkanda passes through the apple belt of Shimla district — a beautiful drive through orchards and pine forests.

name: Friendship Peak Trek

permitInfo.type: HP TMS Registration + Kullu DFO Forest Permit + Mountaineering Permit (IMF/HPMA)
permitInfo.where: HP TMS: trekking.hp.gov.in; IMF/HPMA mountaineering permit: imfindia.com or HPMA Manali (01902-252380); Kullu DFO forest: Manali Range Office
permitInfo.fee: HP TMS mandatory; IMF/HPMA mountaineering permit: ₹500–₹2,000 per person (Indian); ₹5,000+ per person (foreign nationals); Kullu forest entry fee applicable
permitInfo.note: Friendship Peak (5,289m) is classified as a trekking peak by the Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) and requires an IMF or HPMA mountaineering permit in addition to HP TMS registration. This is the most popular beginner mountaineering summit in Himachal Pradesh — a true crampon-and-ice-axe climb, not a trail trek. A licensed and experienced guide is mandatory. Summit success requires two prior acclimatisation nights at high camp. A full technical equipment kit (crampons, ice axe, harness, rope) is required — rental available from Manali gear shops. IMF-affiliated agencies in Manali can arrange combined guide + permit packages.

description: The most popular beginner mountaineering summit in Himachal Pradesh — a 5,289m glacier peak above the Solang Nullah valley that offers a genuine high-altitude climbing experience without extreme technical difficulty. Friendship Peak sits in the Pir Panjal range above Beas Kund, and its ascent involves glacier travel, crampon use, and a 50° snow slope to the summit — making it the ideal first Himalayan summit for trekkers ready to move beyond trail trekking. Views from the top encompass Hanuman Tibba (5,982m), Deo Tibba (6,001m), Indrasan (6,221m), and the Rohtang range.

overview.location: Friendship Peak (5,289m) is in the Pir Panjal range above the Solang Nullah valley, Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh. The approach follows the Beas Kund trail from Solang Nullah (2,480m) through the famous Bakarthach meadows and Beas Kund lake to reach the high camps on the glacier approach. Manali (2,050m) is the base, 14 km from Solang Nullah. The summit commands views of Hanuman Tibba (5,982m), the Rohtang range, the Lahaul peaks, and on clear days the Spiti mountains to the east.
overview.history: Friendship Peak gained its name in the 1950s–60s when Indo-Soviet mountaineering expeditions used the peak for joint climbing exercises during the Indo-Soviet Friendship period — one of several peaks in the Manali region named after diplomatic gestures of the era. The peak was developed as a beginner mountaineering objective by Mountaineering Institutes (ABVIMAS Manali) in the 1970s–80s as a training summit. It remains the most popular IMF-listed trekking peak in Himachal Pradesh, with dozens of teams attempting the summit every May–October season.
overview.length: Approximately 45 km round trip from Solang Nullah to summit and back, over 7–8 days. Elevation gain from Solang (2,480m) to summit (5,289m): 2,809m. The summit day from high camp (4,700m) involves 589m of gain on snow and glacier, taking 4–6 hours in good conditions.
overview.temperature: May–June: −5°C to 10°C at high camp; softer snow; good visibility. September–October: −15°C to 5°C at camp; firmer snow; excellent visibility; coldest nights. Summit wind-chill can drop to −20°C at any time. Thermal layers, down jacket, and windproof outer shell essential throughout.
overview.fitness: Expert/mountaineering level. This is a technical mountaineering objective, not a trail trek. Prior experience on multi-day Himalayan treks is essential. Crampon use, basic rope work, and ice axe technique must be learned before the expedition or taught by your guide on approach days. Strong cardiovascular fitness required — acclimatisation to 4,000m+ before the summit push is mandatory. Not suitable for those without prior high-altitude experience.

itinerary.title: Manali — Solang Nullah — Dhundi
itinerary.desc: Drive from Manali to Solang Nullah ski resort (14 km). Register at the forest check-post (carry HP TMS receipt and IMF permit). Trek from Solang up the Solang Nullah valley to Dhundi — a wide river meadow at the tree line with the Pir Panjal peaks emerging above. Equipment check and crampon familiarisation at camp.

itinerary.title: Dhundi — Bakarthach Meadows
itinerary.desc: The trail climbs through the magnificent Bakarthach meadows — one of the finest wildflower valleys in Himachal. At 3,400m the views of Hanuman Tibba and the Friendship Peak glacier come into view. Acclimatisation afternoon walk to 3,600m recommended.

itinerary.title: Bakarthach — Beas Kund — Lady Leg Camp
itinerary.desc: Pass the sacred Beas Kund lake (3,700m) — source of the Beas River — and continue up the moraine and snow slopes to the glacier base camp known as Lady Leg camp (4,200m). First use of crampons may begin from this section. Crevasse awareness briefing at camp.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation — Glacier Training at Lady Leg Camp
itinerary.desc: Rest and acclimatisation day. Guide conducts crampon technique, ice axe arrest, and rope team movement training on the lower glacier slopes. This training day is mandatory for all participants — summit safety depends on these skills. Afternoon rest.

itinerary.title: Lady Leg Camp — High Camp
itinerary.desc: Move across the glacier to the high camp below the summit headwall. Roped glacier travel through the icefield — crevasses require careful navigation. The high camp at 4,700m is a spectacular snow platform with close views of the summit snowfield. Early dinner and attempt to sleep by 7 PM for the alpine start.

itinerary.title: Summit Day — Friendship Peak 5,289m — Return to Base
itinerary.camp: Lady Leg camp / Bakarthach (4,200m or lower)
itinerary.desc: Alpine start at 3–4 AM with headlamps. The summit push follows the snow ridge and 50° headwall to the summit. Fixed rope used on the steepest section. The summit at 5,289m: Hanuman Tibba and Deo Tibba fill the view to the northwest; the Spiti ranges and Rohtang to the east. Descend carefully back to high camp, retrieve remaining gear, and push down to Lady Leg camp or Bakarthach.

itinerary.title: Return — Bakarthach — Dhundi — Solang — Manali
itinerary.desc: Full descent through the Beas Kund valley and Bakarthach meadows back to Solang Nullah. Drive to Manali. The recovery after the summit push — hot food, hot shower, and the satisfaction of a genuine Himalayan summit.

name: Yunam Peak Trek

permitInfo.type: IMF/HPMA Mountaineering Permit + HP TMS Registration
permitInfo.where: IMF permit: imfindia.com (online) or IMF New Delhi (011-24611211); HPMA Manali: 01902-252380; HP TMS: trekking.hp.gov.in
permitInfo.fee: IMF/HPMA mountaineering permit: ₹1,000–₹2,500 per person (Indian); ₹8,000–₹15,000 per person (foreigners); HP TMS mandatory; Lahaul forest/protected area fee may apply
permitInfo.note: Yunam Peak (6,111m) is an IMF-listed trekking peak in the Lahaul Himalaya and requires an IMF mountaineering permit. At 6,111m, this is a serious high-altitude mountaineering objective — not a beginner summit. Prior experience on 5,000m+ summits is strongly recommended. Technical gear (crampons, ice axe, harness, rope, and fixed line) required throughout. A certified Himalayan guide (IMF Grade A) is mandatory. The approach road via Manali–Leh Highway (NH3) is open only June–September. Base camp at Jispa/Darcha — acclimatisation in Jispa before the glacier approach is essential.

description: One of the most accessible 6,000m peaks in India — Yunam Peak (6,111m) in the Lahaul Himalaya rises dramatically above the Baralacha La area of the Manali–Leh Highway. A serious but achievable high-altitude mountaineering objective for experienced trekkers ready for their first 6,000m summit. The approach through the glaciated Lahaul landscape is spectacular, and the summit commands a 360° view encompassing the entire Lahaul–Spiti watershed, Baralacha La, Suraj Tal, and the peaks of the greater Himalayan chain from Triloknath to the Zaskar range.

overview.location: Yunam Peak (6,111m) rises above the Yunam Nullah in Lahaul district, Himachal Pradesh, near the Baralacha La (4,890m) on the Manali–Leh Highway. Base camp is typically established near Jispa (3,200m) or Darcha (3,360m) on the Bhaga River — both accessible from Manali (110 km) via the Rohtang Pass and Lahaul valley. The summit is on the main Himalayan watershed between the Lahaul and Ladakh regions. Suraj Tal lake (glacial source of the Bhaga River, itself a tributary of the Chenab) is visible from the approach.
overview.history: Yunam Peak was first climbed in the 1950s by Himalayan Club expeditions during the intensive surveying and climbing period that followed Indian independence. The Baralacha La crossroads — at which the routes to Spiti, Ladakh, and Lahaul converge — has been a trade and military route for centuries, used by Lahauli merchants and Changpa nomads alike. The peak became an IMF-listed trekking peak in the 1980s when the Manali–Leh road opened to civilian traffic. At 6,111m, Yunam is prized as one of the few 6,000m objectives that can be attempted from a road-accessible base camp.
overview.length: Approximately 40 km round trip from Jispa to summit and back, over 6–7 days. Elevation gain from Jispa base (3,200m) to summit (6,111m): 2,911m. The summit day from high camp (5,400m) involves 711m of gain on steep snow, ice, and mixed terrain, taking 5–8 hours.
overview.temperature: June–July: −5°C to 10°C at base camp; glacier soft; good weather windows. August: −8°C to 5°C at high camps; most stable weather. September: −15°C to 2°C; firmest snow; coldest nights; best visibility. Summit temperature with wind chill: −25°C to −35°C possible. Full high-altitude mountaineering clothing system essential.
overview.fitness: Expert/mountaineering. Prior experience on a 5,000m+ summit is strongly recommended. Good acclimatisation (minimum 2 nights at 3,500m+ before the glacier push) is mandatory. Strong cardiovascular fitness over sustained effort at altitude. Technical skills: crampon technique, ice axe self-arrest, basic rope management, roped glacier travel. Not suitable for first-time high-altitude trekkers.

itinerary.title: Manali — Rohtang Pass — Jispa Base Camp
itinerary.desc: Drive from Manali over Rohtang Pass (3,978m) and down through the Lahaul valley — the dramatic descent from the green Kullu valley into the arid grey-and-brown Lahaul moonscape. Pass Keylong (Lahaul district HQ) and continue to Jispa on the banks of the Bhaga River. Register permits at the check-post. Acclimatisation walk in the evening. Jispa at 3,200m is a critical first night for altitude adjustment.

itinerary.title: Jispa — Darcha — Glacier Approach Camp
itinerary.desc: From Darcha (3,360m), leave the highway and enter the Yunam Nullah. The trail follows the nullah through increasingly barren Lahaul terrain — brown rock, glacial streams, and the first views of the Yunam snowfields. Reach the glacier approach camp at 3,800m. Full technical equipment check by guide.

itinerary.title: Acclimatisation — Advance Base Camp
itinerary.desc: Carry loads to Advance Base Camp at 4,600m on the lower glacier margins. The terrain becomes increasingly rocky and snow-covered. Practice crampon technique on easy snow slopes above ABC. Return to lower camp if altitude causes symptoms, or sleep at ABC if acclimatised.

itinerary.title: Advance Base Camp — Camp 1 on Glacier
itinerary.desc: Fully roped glacier travel begins. The Yunam glacier is crevassed in the middle section — guide sets the route and marks the line. Camp 1 at 5,100m is established on a flattened snow platform. Altitude symptoms monitored closely. Early sleep for the high camp push tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Camp 1 — High Camp
itinerary.desc: Short but steep carry to High Camp at 5,400m. The slope steepens considerably — fixed rope sections placed by guide. At 5,400m the wind is constant and temperatures drop sharply. High calorie food and maximum hydration before tomorrow's summit push. Full gear prepared tonight: crampons on, harness fitted, ice axe ready. Sleep by 7 PM.

itinerary.title: Summit Day — Yunam Peak 6,111m — Full Descent to Base
itinerary.desc: Alpine start at 2–3 AM. The summit pyramid is climbed on steep mixed snow/rock — ice axe technique and crampon work essential in the final 400m. The 6,111m summit: a profound panorama of the entire Lahaul–Spiti–Ladakh watershed. Baralacha La, Suraj Tal, the Zaskar range, and distant Kullu peaks all visible in clear conditions. Controlled descent on fixed ropes. Full descent to base camp or Darcha by evening.

itinerary.title: Darcha — Manali Return
itinerary.desc: Drive back through Lahaul and over Rohtang to Manali. The post-summit return through the dramatic Lahaul landscape feels very different after a 6,111m summit. Permit documentation to be completed in Manali.
